_comment: This file is managed by the todo CLI. Do not edit it directly, by hand or with a script. Read it with todo: `todo next --json` (what to work on), `todo show --id <id|ref> --json` (one task), `todo list --flat` (every item as flat JSON records). Change it with todo commands (add, edit, move, status, assign, rm, ...; see `todo --help`), which keep its ids and rules valid.

categories.title: Decide before 1.0 (schema changes are free until then)

tasks.title: Artist page lists a collection album under Albums when the artist only has a song on it
tasks.description: If an artist has a song on a collection (soundtrack, compilation), the album shows under the artist's Albums although it should not. Check whether it still reproduces after the "Appears on" split (`splitAppearances`, `getArtist`) and the groupings work, and fix what is left.

tasks.title: Play-queue saves break when the queue holds a radio station
tasks.description:
Fix these whichever direction "Radio stations in the play queue" (Decide before 1.0) takes — they are wrong under both options.
(a) The client's `currentIndex` counts the dropped radio entry, so a station before the playing track makes `currentIndex >= len(trackIDs)` and `savePlayQueueByIndex` answers error 10 (`subsonic/playqueue.go:73`) — discarding the whole save, tracks included; a station after it nominates the wrong current track.
(b) A radio-only queue decodes to zero ids, which routes to `clearSavedQueue` (`playqueue.go:58`) and deletes the other device's saved session.
Minor: `usePlayer.ts:74` scrobbles `radio-<name>`, which answers `invalid id` (log noise only).
Root cause: a station enters the queue as a synthetic `Song` (`webui/src/utils/radioSong.ts:8` — `id: radio-<name>` plus a `streamUrl`, deliberately not the real `rs-<n>`). `useQueueSync.pushQueue` (`webui/src/composables/useQueueSync.ts:50`) sends `queue.map(s => s.id)` verbatim, and the backend's `decodeTrackIDs` (`subsonic/playlists.go:249`) silently drops every non-`tr-` id.

tasks.title: `image-source` can report `folder` while `/rest` serves the generated avatar
tasks.description: `GET /api/v0/artists/{id}/image-source` inspects the disk itself, while `/rest/getCoverArt` goes through the media path guard. When the on-disk artist image is refused by the guard — always with zero scan folders configured, and when the image FILE itself is a symlink that resolves outside every root — the endpoint says `folder`, so the artist page's edit note reads e.g. "artist.jpg — from music folder" while the image actually shown is the generated avatar. Make `image-source` ask the same guard (or fold it into the per-root health gate).

tasks.title: Album cover Remove cannot tell whether there is anything to remove
tasks.description: `AlbumView`'s hero Remove clears aether's managed cover via `updateAlbum`'s `coverClear`, but most albums are served from folder art or embedded tags — so Remove → Save deletes a non-existent asset entry and the old cover reappears. Mitigated only by helper text today. `HeroHeader` already has a `coverRemovable` prop, and `ArtistView` drives it from an image-source query (`canRemoveImage`). The album equivalent needs `/rest` to report whether the served cover is aether-managed — an OpenSubsonic extension field or small endpoint, not an `/api/v0` route, since album covers are music functionality. Same gap exists for genres.

tasks.title: Identify album sometimes assigns the wrong track position
tasks.description: In the metadata editor, identifying an album sometimes puts tracks at the wrong position. Find where the match → position mapping goes wrong and improve it. (Listed twice in the old TODO, under 1.0 and Future releases.)

tasks.title: Per-root health gate for scan folders
tasks.description: A cached, single-flight "is this root answering" state that everything consults before touching a scan folder's directory: the media handlers (`stream`, `getCoverArt`), the metadata-editor handlers, the scan preflight and `/api/v0/libraries/browse`. Today only `GET /api/v0/scan-folders` and the startup warning are bounded (`Folder.AvailableWithin`, single-flight per root); everything else stats a dead mount directly, so a hung NFS/SMB share costs one blocked request per call, the scan preflight's `Available()` is unbounded — a wedged scan cannot be cancelled and holds the `library-writes` exclusion group, so editor re-indexes and `prune` queue behind it — and the editor spins forever. One gate closes all three. Rule to keep: bound the RESOURCE, not only the wait (goroutine + timeout alone pins one OS thread per timed-out probe).

tasks.title: Re-link rows that no scan folder walks any more
tasks.description: Changing a scan folder's `Path` keeps its rows (ids, stars, playlists, history) only if the OLD location is gone when the next scan runs — the move proof needs ENOENT at the old path. The careful migration (copy to a new disk, repoint, verify, delete the old copy later) therefore re-links nothing: new rows are created and the old ones are swept, silently. Fix: treat rows that no configured folder walks any more as re-link candidates — after preflight every walk is in memory, so every folder's `BulkMarkSeen` can run before the first reconcile; a row still at `last_seen_at < scanStart` is doomed whether or not its file exists, which makes it a sound candidate. The condition is documented in `config.yaml` and `docs/agents/scanning.md` and pinned by a scanner test.

tasks.title: Record a logical (as-spelled) path per track — fixes tracks reached through symlinks not playing
tasks.description: CONFIRMED defect: with `FollowSymlinks`, content reached through a symlink is recorded under its RESOLVED path. When that path lies outside every scan folder root the track is indexed but does not play: `stream` answers "song not found" and on-disk/embedded cover art is refused, because `pathguard` resolves the path and checks containment. The same missing column is behind: a library `path` filter on or below a symlink matching nothing; a scan folder whose ROOT is a symlink being refused outright (`Folder.Available()`); the editor's spelled→resolved mapping; the metadata editor not listing symlinked directories at all; and the scan's second guard having no path-range backup for symlink-reached rows. Fix: store the path as spelled next to the resolved one; for follow-symlinks folders the guard becomes lexical containment of the spelled path. `RescanPaths`' availability guard must stay until this replaces it. Workaround today: list the link's target as a scan folder of its own. Analysis: `docs/architecture/caveats.md#content-reached-through-a-symlink-that-leaves-every-scan-folder`.

tasks.title: XML response format for third-party clients
tasks.description: Check compatibility with third-party Subsonic clients (DSub, Ultrasonic, Symfonium, etc.). XML is what several clients default to, so this gates the "third-party clients work" promise. Today `f=xml` is explicitly rejected (`subsonic/subsonic.go`), so those clients fail at the first request. The handlers build `map[string]any` throughout (`albumToMap`, `trackToChild`, …), which does not marshal to spec-shaped XML — this needs a serialization layer, not a flag.

tasks.title: setRating: persist ratings, or stop answering OK for a dropped write
tasks.description: `setRating` is a two-line `writeResponse(w, nil)` (`subsonic/annotation.go`) and no model carries a rating field. The handler answers OK for a write it drops — before 1.0 either add a rating column to tracks/albums or make the response honest.

tasks.title: Index `track_artists` / `album_artists` by `artist_id`
tasks.description: The all-libraries artist index with any hide-artists library takes ~6.7 s at 100k tracks (measured). Cause: a `SCAN` of `track_artists`, which only has its `(track_id, artist_id)` autoindex. Fix: an index leading with `artist_id` on both join tables (`model.Migrate` already hand-writes one raw index).

tasks.title: Better list view
tasks.description: Improve the library list view. Needs scoping: name what is wrong with it today before planning.

tasks.title: Adopt `--app-danger` for the remaining hard-coded error reds (dark-theme contrast)
tasks.description: Error text is coloured per component with PrimeVue palette tokens or a literal hex (`--p-red-500` / `-600` / `-700`), which do not flip with the theme — and no single red passes WCAG AA on both grounds (4.5:1 floor). `--app-danger` (`#b91c1c` light / `#f87171` dark, `webui/src/assets/scss/_variables.scss`) measures 5.4–6.8:1 in both themes. Still hard-coded — TEXT rules only (grep `--p-red-` and `#ef4444` under `webui/src`): `ScheduleDialog.vue`, `metadata-editor/TrackList.vue`, `RawEditPanel.vue`, `IdentifyReviewDialog.vue`, `IdentifyAlbumDialog.vue`, `UserSettingsView.vue`'s `.tone-stale`, `UserMenu.vue`'s `.menu-item.danger`, and the literal `#ef4444` of `.error` in `AlbumView.vue`, `ArtistView.vue`, `GenreDetailView.vue`, `PlaylistDetailView.vue` plus `.clear-btn:hover` in `MusicBrainzAlbumPicker.vue` and `MusicBrainzArtistPicker.vue`. Not bugs, leave them: banners with their own light background (`FolderPickerDialog.vue`, `FolderTree.vue`), and `LoginView.vue`'s `.login-error` on the always-dark login card.

tasks.title: Favorites schema: commit to a per-type split or close as won't-do
tasks.description: Today: junction table `starred_items` keyed `(owner, item_type, item_id)` with unique index `idx_starred_item`; it works. A per-type split (`album_stars`, `artist_stars`, `track_stars`) with `(user_id, item_id)` PKs and cascade deletes is optional. With no consumers a schema change costs only a DB drop — after 1.0 it needs a real migration. So decide now: either do the split while it is cheap or close this; "later" is the one answer that gets expensive.

tasks.title: Radio stations in the play queue: follow the spec, or author a `radioQueue` extension
tasks.description:
Radio stations are not persisted in the play queue across sessions/devices. OpenSubsonic has no mechanism for it: `savePlayQueue`'s `id`/`current` are song ids only, `PlayQueue.entry` is an array of `Child` with a MUST that `current` be a song in the list, and `Child.type`/`mediaType` have no stream/radio value. No registry extension covers it. `model.PlayQueueEntry.TrackID uint` is track-only, and restore rebuilds entries from `model.Track`, so nothing radio-shaped can round-trip.
(A) Follow the spec — radio does not persist cross-device; the client strips non-track entries and recomputes `currentIndex` over the survivors. Pure bugfix, no schema change.
(B) Author a `radioQueue` extension — polymorphic `PlayQueueEntry` (kind + ref), `rs-` ids accepted on the `ByIndex` variant only, spec-shaped `getPlayQueue` still filtered to songs. The schema half is free right now, so weigh B on the spec deviation alone.
Either way, the "Play-queue saves break when the queue holds a radio station" bug comes first.

tasks.title: Should a filtered library's Artists tab honour OTHER hide-artists libraries?
tasks.description: `excludeHiddenArtists` runs only for a zero scope — the all-libraries index, and a library without filters — never inside a filtered library. Inside a FILTERED library, artists whose every track sits in some other hide-artists library are still listed when the two views overlap. Either apply the exclusion there too, or state that "hide artists" means "hide from the global index only". Recorded in `docs/architecture/caveats.md#libraries-are-filters-the-edges-that-come-with-it`.

tasks.title: Extend the OpenAPI response-contract test to the upstream-mocked and uncovered endpoints
tasks.description: `app/router/openapi_response_contract_test.go` validates real handler responses against `docs/openapi/aether-v0.yaml`, but only for endpoints reachable with an in-memory store — bootstrap, auth/tokens, libraries, users, tasks. Closing the gap requires mocking the radio-browser and MusicBrainz upstreams (`internal/radiobrowser`, `internal/artistimage.MusicBrainzSearch`) so `searchRadioStations`, `getRadioFavicon`, `searchMusicBrainzArtists`, `searchMusicBrainzReleases`, `getReleaseGroupGenres`, `listArtistImageCandidates` and `setArtistImageFromSearch` can be asserted offline. Still uncovered beyond that: identify/identify-album fixtures (sample audio plus a fake AcoustID backend), the whole `metadata` group, binary responses (their JSON error paths), and the update/delete/patch mutation variants (`updateTracks`, `clearPictureSelection`, `deleteArtistImage`, `deleteToken`, `deleteUser`, `deleteLibrary`, `patchTaskSchedule`, `deleteTaskSchedule`, `cancelTaskExecution`).

tasks.title: Artists tab — grouped page instead of card grid + drill-down
tasks.description: Replace the grid-of-artist-cards + drill-down with a single scrollable page grouped by artist: one header per artist (alphabetical), followed by that artist's albums sorted by year; no per-artist navigation step. Today `ArtistGrid.vue`/`ArtistListView.vue` cards are `router-link`s to the `artist` route.

tasks.description: MusicBrainz-style sort tags — ArtistSort/AlbumSort/TitleSort/AlbumArtistSort/ComposerSort (`TSOP`/`TSOA`/`TSOT`/`TSO2`/`TSOC`) — control browse ordering. Not read today, so it needs scanner read + a store column + the editor field, not just the write side.

tasks.title: Track comments — decide the editing policy first
tasks.description: COMMENT is a standard tag (ID3 `COMM`, Vorbis `COMMENT`, MP4 `©cmt`), but `go-taglib` reads every tag through TagLib's property map, which flattens comments to one `COMMENT` key: it drops language and description, and cannot tell apart the labelled comments apps stash private data in (e.g. iTunes' `iTunNORM`). A naive "Comment" box could edit the wrong comment, erase hidden app data, or collapse several comments into one. A safe minimal design is to only ever read/write the unlabelled "main" comment and leave labelled frames untouched — a deliberate policy call. Investigated 2026-08-23.

tasks.title: Negated library filters (`not in`)
tasks.description: Every filter but `compilation` is positive only: "everything except audiobooks" needs every other genre listed. Add a per-filter `negate` flag (`ScopeOf` wraps the clause in `NOT (…)`); revisit the "a hide-artists library needs at least one filter" rule and the dangling-scan-folder warning with it. Shape changes are free pre-1.0.

tasks.title: Key owner columns on `User.ID` and re-enable user rename
tasks.description: Per-user scoping of queue, stars, playlists and history has landed (owner-keyed schemas, PAT layer). Remaining: `owner` is still the LOGIN string (`patIdentityResolver` returns `info.LoginID`, `app/router/main.go`), so a rename would orphan queue/stars/playlists/history. Contained today: renaming is refused with 400 (`errRenameUnsupported`, `handlers/users/users.go`) and `UserDialog.vue` shows the login read-only. Re-key the owner columns on `User.ID`, then lift the refusal.

tasks.description: Identify formats browsers cannot play natively and add FFmpeg transcoding. Browsers handle FLAC/MP3/OGG/Opus/AAC, so this is for exotic formats and bandwidth-limited remote listening — a whole subsystem (ffmpeg dependency, cache, per-client profiles).

tasks.title: CUE sheet support
tasks.description: Single audio file + `.cue` sidecar (DJ mixes, EAC FLAC/APE rips), exposed as regular per-track albums with seamless web-UI playback: virtual tracks (file + time region), scanner pairing, ffmpeg remux slicing for third-party clients, an OpenSubsonic extension for region offsets. Full assessment: `docs/cue-playing.md`.

tasks.title: Bookmarks for per-track offsets
tasks.description: Not needed for resume: `savePlayQueue`'s `position` covers it. Only worth adding for offsets that survive a queue replacement (audiobooks, long sets). If added, the play queue stays the single source of truth for the current track's position — do not write both on the same tick.

tasks.title: Scrobble to ListenBrainz / Last.fm
tasks.description: Forward each play off-box. Nothing outbound exists today: the browser applies Last.fm's 50%/4min/30s rule (`usePlayer.ts`), calls `/rest/scrobble`, and the server appends to `play_history` (`subsonic/annotation.go`). Prerequisites: the `submission` parameter is ignored, so now-playing pings are recorded as completed plays; and there is no user/settings table to hold a session key. Consider ListenBrainz first — one unsigned POST with a token, no signed handshake or app registration. Last.fm adds `track.love`/`artist.getInfo`/`album.getInfo` on the same key.

tasks.title: Metadata editor picture previews in the desktop app
tasks.description: Picture previews and the artist image build URLs from `apiClient.defaults.baseURL`, and copy-picture calls a raw fetch (`webui/src/lib/api/Metadata.ts`, `PicturesSection.vue`). The `/api/v0` picture endpoints are cookie-authenticated, so none of it loads in the app. Fix: fetch through the host transport (`httpFetch`) and render object URLs — the window CSP already admits `blob:`. Then give `originAgnostic.spec.ts` a third rule: no raw `fetch(`/`sendBeacon(`/`axios.create(` outside the transport (`savePlayQueueBeacon`'s `sendBeacon` being the sanctioned exception).

tasks.title: Re-check the PrimeVue `Select` Escape quirk on the next PrimeVue upgrade
tasks.description: PrimeVue 4.5.5's `Select.onEscapeKey` calls `stopPropagation()` even when its overlay is closed, so while a `Select` holds focus Escape never reaches a hosting `Dialog`. Documented in `docs/agents/frontend.md` ("A focused `Select` swallows Escape"), deliberately not worked around. On upgrade, check whether upstream fixed it and delete that paragraph if so.
